text:
maria: Heads-up — kicking off planning for a new Dedicated feature were calling 'burst pockets' (working name). Goal: give customers a small, billable burst buffer on top of reserved capacity that preserves SLAs but lets them absorb short traffic spikes. Need scope, launch criteria, and engineering estimate. :eyes:
aj: high level sounds good. couple constraints: GPU memory and KV cache sizing are the tricky bits for short bursts. we should avoid per-request cold KV fills for pockets or cost will blow up.
tess: can we define minimal launch docs now? runbook + pricing + console toggle + basic dashboard. without that we cant ship.
ryan: a few enterprise customers asked for something like this but price sensitivity is high. they want a predictable flat monthly buffer rather than per-token surges. may be two pricing paths: prepaid pocket vs pay-as-you-burst.
kai: ops concerns: isolation & noisy neighbor protection. we need an eviction heuristic and a graceful fallback path to reserved capacity or hosted model. also meter at token-level per-customer for billing.
maria: sketch of proposal: (1) single "pocket" SKU per customer (small fixed compute slots + token allowance), (2) soft-reserve fraction on each dedicated instance so pockets don't evict reserved requests, (3) automatic fallback to pinned model variant (lower-cost) if pocket exhausted. Thoughts?
aj: +1 to soft-reserve. implementation note: soft-reserve = we mark X% of GPU threads as reserved for committed customers; pockets can use unused soft-reserve when idle but will be preempted. preemption must be O(1) to avoid blocking scheduling.
kai: suggested eviction policy: "soft-reserve preempt" then LRU across pocket-sessions. also we should avoid killing in-flight responses; instead allow finish-of-current-turn then preempt.
ryan: messaging suggestion: "burst pockets give you X extra QPS for short spikes, charged as a monthly pocket or per-minute consumption". need example cost math in the PRD.
tess: launch checklist draft (short):
- PRD + pricing table
- feature flag + console toggle
- billing integration + test invoices
- dashboard with pocket usage (p95/p99 spikes)
- runbook for Ops + customer support playbook
- 2 customer beta trials
please add anything missing.
oncall-bot: REMINDER: create incident runbook entry for pocket preemption scenarios before beta. (auto-generated)
maria: MVP scope proposal (quarter):
- Core scheduler support for pockets (single SKU)
- Token-level metering + billing hook (test invoices)
- Eviction policy: soft-reserve preempt then LRU finish-current-turn
- Fallback route to pinned lower-cost model variant
- Console UI: enable/disable + usage graph
- Docs + runbook + 2 customer betas
Stretch: dynamic cross-region pooling, per-route pockets, prepaid monthly SKUs.
aj: rough estimate: core scheduler + eviction logic = 4w, metering + billing + tests = 3w, console + docs + beta infra = 2w. end-to-end ~9w with one engineering pod. with parallel work across infra & frontend maybe 7w.
kai: infra ask: need a temporary 4 GPU test pool and billing sandbox. budget request ~ 12k for Q.
maria: proposed launch acceptance criteria (simple):
- pocket provisioning API + console toggle works end-to-end
- billing records show pocket usage and invoice items in sandbox
- p99 latency for reserved requests unchanged within 5% during pocket bursts in beta
- runbook for preemption + support playbook validated with 2 betas
- monitoring: pocket usage, preempt count, evictions, fallback rate
if we clear these, we go to GA.
ryan: agree on criteria. can we add one customer-facing SLA statement for GA? maybe: "no impact to reserved SLA for customers with pockets enabled" — but legal will want clearer wording.
tess: timeline ask: if eng says 7w, would like to schedule beta in week 9 so marketing + CS can prep.
aj: tagging timeline: start SOW next monday -> sprint 1 scheduler + tests, sprint 2 metering + billing, sprint 3 console + beta. unblockers: infra pool + billing sandbox.
maria: action items: @aj please confirm final eng ETA by EOD tomorrow, @kai please start budget req & test pool request, @tess please draft beta support playbook and PRD pricing appendix. i'll assemble acceptance criteria into PRD once eng ETA is in. :rocket:
